newsitem.title: USA: NBA-TIMBERWOLVES ON TRAIL OF FIRST PLAYOFF BERTH.
newsitem.headline: NBA-TIMBERWOLVES ON TRAIL OF FIRST PLAYOFF BERTH.

text.p: Tom Gugliotta's 12-foot jumper with 16 seconds left was the clincher as the Timberwolves scored the last 10 points of the game Friday to beat the Washington Bullets 97-95 and inch closer to a playoff berth.

Kevin Garnett scored 22 points to lead the Timberwolves, who reduced their magic number for clinching a playoff berth to one. The Wolves will earn their first-ever post-season berth with one more win or one loss by the Sacramento Kings.
"We have shown the ability to stick around in games and execute down the stretch," Minnesota coach Flip Saunders said. "We wanted to keep ourselves in the position to win the game and we did that."

Juwan Howard and Rod Strickland both had 21 points for the Bullets, who had their six-game winning streak snapped but remained tied with the Cleveland Cavaliers for the final playoff berth in the Eastern Conference.
"The Timberwolves played great," Strickland said. "They put the heat on."
In Atlanta, Christian Laettner scored 12 of his 30 points in the third quarter as the Hawks defeated Detroit 103-89 to move into a tie with the Pistons for fourth place in the Eastern Conference.
Atlanta beat the Pistons for the first time in four meetings this seasons. Detroit had been the only team the Hawks had not defeated.
The Hawks, winners of eight of their last nine, moved within one game of New York for third spot in the East after the Knicks lost to Orlando. Atlanta hosts New York Saturday.
Mookie Blaylock recorded 21 points, 11 rebounds and eight assists for the Hawks, who improved to 34-4 at the Omni.
Detroit's Grant Hill had his second straight triple-double and third in four games with 22 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists.
In Chicago, Scottie Pippen shook off a horrendous first half to make 6-of-7 shots in scoring 15 third-quarter points as the Chicago Bulls defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 84-71.

Pippen, 0-for-7 from the floor in the first half, keyed a 13-2 burst early in the third quarter and another 10-2 run near the end of the period. Michael Jordan led Chicago with 22 points, but had just eight after the half.
The league-best Bulls improved to 64-10.
Tyrone Hill had 18 points to lead Cleveland.

The Bulls played without their top reserve, forward Toni Kukoc, who re-injured his right foot before the game. But they got a much-needed lift with the debut of recently signed forward Brian Williams, who had six points and two rebounds.
In New York, Penny Hardaway scored 23 points and had a pair of buckets during a key third-quarter burst that lifted the hobbled Orlando Magic past the New York Knicks 93-84.
The Magic won on the road despite playing without guard Dennis Scott, who has a strained knee, and Seikaly, who sprained an ankle in Thursday's loss to the Clippers.
Orlando is seventh in the Eastern Conference, 2 1/2 games ahead of Cleveland. New York is third in the East, but fell 3 1/2 games behind Miami in the Atlantic Division.
Larry Johnson had 25 points and 17 rebounds for the Knicks, who are 5-6 in their last 11 games.
In Denver, Kevin Johnson scored 24 points as the surging Phoenix Suns beat the Denver Nuggets 122-113.
The Suns, writing an improbable story after opening the season 0-13, have won eight straight and occupy the seventh playoff spot in the Western Conference.
Antonio McDyess had 26 points to pace Denver.
At Utah, Karl Malone scored 16 points in just 22 minutes as the Utah Jazz overwhelmed the Vancouver Grizzlies 106-79 in a matchup of the Western Conference's best and worst teams.
Malone's first bucket allowed him to become the first NBA player to reach the 2,000-point mark in 10 straight seasons.

In Boston, Lamond Murray came off the bench to score 24 points as the Los Angeles Clippers' reserves outscored their Boston counterparts by nearly 60 points in a 117-102 defeat of the reeling Celtics.
Rookie Antoine Walker scored 36 points for Boston (13-62).
In Philadelphia, Travis Best scored 27 points as the Indiana Pacers defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 114-103.
In Portland, Isaiah Rider scored 27 points as the Trail Blazers beat the Milwaukee Bucks 108-93.
Portland holds a comfortable 6 1/2-game lead over Minnesota for the fifth spot in the Western Conference playoff race and needs one win to clinch it.
In Los Angeles, Dominique Wilkins scored 28 points as the San Antonio Spurs beat the injury-depleted Los Angeles Lakers 94-83, snapping their five-game winning streak.
In Sacramento, Charles Barkley scored 20 points and grabbed 12 rebounds as the Houston Rockets completed a dominant season sweep of the Kings with a 108-94 victory.
Hakeem Olajuwon led the Rockets with 25 points and Clyde Drexler added 20 for Houston. Barkley was playing his second game since missing 14 with a hip injury.
